summary: A satirical article dated September 27, 2023 that mocks endpoint security practices among remote workers. It walks through passwords, antivirus, firewalls, VPNs, patch management, encryption, security training, backups and security audits, each illustrated by a comically named employee who fails at basic security. It concludes that endpoint security strategies need more substance than "a laugh track and crossed fingers."
one_line: A humorous September 2023 satire lampooning remote workers' poor endpoint security habits, from weak passwords and skipped patches to useless training and missing backups.
key_facts: The article is dated September 27, 2023 and satirizes endpoint security in the age of remote work.
John "I clicked the link" Doe of the hacked DoGood Corp admitted his password was "Password123", which hackers cracked in 0.003 seconds.
Ethel "The Firewall" Harris argues that having antivirus is as essential as having a door on a bathroom stall.
Antivirus software is compared to a digital scarecrow that often seems to be on break when real attacks arrive.
Tim "The Trojan" Henderson from Accounting clicked a pop-up promising a free iPhone, defeating the firewall's protection.
Gerard "Incognito" Flynn bought his VPN service at a "killer discount" after the fifth pop-up ad, and his online activity was reportedly exposed when the VPN failed.
Margaret "Update Later" Thompson's unpatched device became the entry point for a vicious attack.
Barry "Barely Cares" Gunderson sent company secrets over insecure Wi-Fi, showing the lax attitude toward encryption.
Sandra "Skipped the Seminar" Smith used the "I thought it was legit" defense despite mandatory security training, which is mocked as ineffective click-through slides.
Jack "Just this once I didn't" Daniels lost his project because he had no backup.
Mildred "Missed the Memo" Beasley accidentally left a digital door ajar, illustrating that security audits are tick-box exercises.
The article closes by saying endpoint security strategies need more than "a laugh track and crossed fingers."
